name: THE BOUNDARY MAN
note: Doc 07 #2 and #3, the one doc 07 marks A (Clement, by B's R_BORDERS_MOTT). The two have argued about the same forty feet for six years; they stand in the middle of the street, facing each other. TALK TO either opens the one tree, and they answer alternately (errata 110). Errata 193 (Tyler, 2026-11-08): moved off Main Street to the claim row, where they stand facing each other on the near edge of the claims, each beside a marker's post (A by THE MOTHERLODE's, B by PROVIDENCE's), below the boards and clear of every marker's approach point.
greetsWithBarkNote: As the card sharp: TALK TO opens with the pair's bark for the current reputation, in both voices.

R_SWINDLED.speaker: boundary_b
R_SWINDLED.line: Sold you Claim Two? Ha! That's not even disputed.

R_RACCOON.speaker: boundary_a
R_RACCOON.line: At least yours has an animal on it.

R_SURVEYED.speaker: boundary_a
R_SURVEYED.line: Don't. Don't put ideas in it.

R_LOST_DUEL.speaker: boundary_b
R_LOST_DUEL.line: We could've told you not to duel Vessel.

barksNote: EXTRACTED from docs/07-ambient-layer.md (## 2 & 3 · THE TWO BOUNDARY MEN) by tools/extract-content.mjs, as `barkExchange`: the table is written in two voices, each line said over its own man. Directions are dropped (errata 110).

sprite.frameNote: 0 rest, arms folded, facing B · 1 breath (derived) · 2 points across the forty feet · 3 argues, hand raised -- TALK. B breaks on the same 10 s cycle half a cycle later (phase 0.5), so the two never point on the same beat.
sprite.figureHeightNote: Crown to sole (errata 112 L), the brim read by eye from the rest frame's row widths: tools/art/figure-height.py --hat took his folded arms for the brim (errata 115).
sprite.rateNote: Errata 273 (Tyler, 2026-11-10: "The man seems to be breathing rapidly (shoulders rising and falling too quickly)"): 0.4, was 0.55. A breath at rest is a slow thing; tests/movement.test.mjs holds a standing person's breath to 0.5 a second at most.

walkToNote: Beside them at their own depth, not in front (Tyler, 2026-11-07: "Thad's line hit the tops of the heads of the boundary men when he talks to them"). Stood nearer the camera, his words rose from a head lower on the screen than theirs and ran across their hats; level with them, his words sit above all three heads. Was 1700,830. Errata 187: from their right now, at the same depth -- the hitching horses (full-sized, Tyler 2026-11-08) stand in the near mud in front of where their left side was, and a horse's head would have covered him there. Errata 193: on the claim row, still from their right at their own depth (885,625), the same distance from B for the room's larger man, clear of every marker's approach point.
whenNote: Errata 189: up the hill on the funeral day (doc 57 C3: 'The street is half empty. Everyone in town who owns a black coat is up the hill.'). Four of Main Street's eight townspeople go -- the boundary men, the letter-writer and the pie woman; the map seller, the man leaving tomorrow, the message boy and the dog's owner stay, each for the reason their one joke gives. Errata 193 moved the pair to the claim row and kept this condition: they are up the hill on the funeral day wherever they stand.
